ITEM.PTXT: When driving force is generated at the rear wheels during acceleration, etc., the load on the front and rear wheels changes due to inertia. As a result, the load on the rear wheels increases and the rear of the vehicle squats. In anti-squat geometry, the geometric intersection point (OR) of the suspension is brought closer to the axle center; when the reaction force (T) of the driving force acting on the axle center tries to move the vehicle forward via the intersection point (OR), because there is an angle between the reaction force of the driving force and the direction of the intersection point, component forces are generated in the direction of the intersection point (T1) and in the direction of the ground contact surface (T2). By reducing this component force in the direction of the ground contact surface, squat at the rear of the vehicle during acceleration is suppressed.
